candidate.title: A Quadratic-Advice Two-Block Sponge Collision Attack with Preprocessing
candidate.subtitle: Lifting the multi-instance attack to the auxiliary-input random permutation model
candidate.one_line: Whether the multi-instance two-block sponge collision attack of advantage (S^2 T^4 / C^2)^S lifts to an auxiliary-input attack of advantage S^2 T^4 / C^2, matching the best proved security bound.
candidate.status_note: Settled in the multi-instance model by the paper's Theorem 3 (advantage (Omega-tilde(S^2 T^4 / C^2))^S). Open in the auxiliary-input model, which is what the paper asks for; no partial result there is reported.
candidate.progress_note: The paper's Theorem 2 proves the O-tilde(ST/C + S^2 T^4 / C^2 + T^2/min(C,R)) bound whose middle term is the target, and its Theorem 3 shows that term cannot be removed by the multi-instance technique because an MI attack reaches it.
risks: The side condition S^2 T^4 <= C^2 is a formalization choice, not in the paper, imposed so the claim is about a probability; flagged in a remark.
The paper phrases this as a question with 'suggests' and 'may'; the page reproduces both hedges rather than removing them.
The MI-to-AI lift is not a general principle; the statement asserts only its conclusion in this one case, and says so.

verify.reason: The question is posed in the paper's open-problems section and the multi-instance half is a theorem of the paper, so the asymmetry the statement asserts is real. The repairs concern the statement's form rather than its content: an advantage stated as S^2 T^4 / C^2 needs a range to be a probability, and the paper's hedges must survive.

checks.finding: Posed in section 1.3 under the heading 'Better attacks for B = 2?', p. 9.

The paper gives the MI attack (Theorem 3, restated as Theorem 11 in section 5) and asks for the AI analogue; no section of the paper supplies one, and its own Table 1 lists the best known B=2 attack as ST/C + T^2/min(C,R), not S^2 T^4 / C^2.

The paper's target is Omega(S^2 T^4 / C^2) with no range. Stated unrestricted it asserts a probability can exceed one. Corrected by the side condition S^2 T^4 <= C^2, flagged in remark rem:sidecondition as a formalization choice.

Theorem 3's side condition S, T, R >= 16 is carried over verbatim into the statement's Theorem 1; the MI game samples salts without replacement, as the paper's Definition 5 does, and the statement's Definition 3 says so.

The MI attack and the security bound whose term it matches are both the source paper's. The attack whose optimality would be refuted is FGK22's, and the MD comparison is attributed to ACDW20 and AGL22.

Sponge, the AI game and the MI game reproduce the paper's section 2.3 and Definitions 2, 3 and 5. The MI adversary's statefulness across rounds - the feature the hardness discussion turns on - is stated, as the paper does.

The first draft asserted the AI attack exists. The paper says the bound 'suggests that there may exist' one and then asks a question. Corrected: remark rem:attribution reproduces both hedges and records that the direction is a reading.
Definitions 1-3 give the construction and both games, so a solver knows exactly which model the attack must live in and which one it may not.
